messages.author: de2c0368d9349f5a
messages.subject: Multidimensional IRT models
parts:
Hi,

I got a 22 item test and I am trying to fit a two dimensional irt model. The related syntax is:

model.priorM2 <- mirt.model('F1 = 1-22,
                             F2 = 1-22,
                             PRIOR = (1-22, d, norm, 0, 1),
                             PRIOR = (1-22, a1, lnorm, 0.5306283, 0.8143413),
                             PRIOR = (1-22, a2, lnorm, 0.5306283, 0.8143413)')


resultM2<-mirt(respcorM1,model=model.priorM2,itemtype='3PL',
                           SE=TRUE,method="EM")

However, the "discrimination" parameter estimates are the same, within each item:

$i1
             a1      a2      d     g  u
par       1.798   1.798 -0.569 0.109  1
CI_2.5  -20.083 -20.083 -1.245 0.042 NA
CI_97.5  23.680  23.680  0.107 0.253 NA

$i2
             a1      a2      d     g  u
par       1.273   1.273 -1.114 0.095  1
CI_2.5  -14.211 -14.211 -1.991 0.027 NA
CI_97.5  16.757  16.757 -0.238 0.285 NA

.
.
.

I am aware about the issues concerning the model identification of multidimensional IRT models. However, since the factors are assumed to be uncorrelated, their means and variances were set o be 0 and 1, respectively and, due to the prior choice of the "discrimination" parameters, which lead to their estimates will be always positive, the model would be already identified and no longer restrictions would be necessary (http://www.ime.unicamp.br/sites/default/files/pesquisa/relatorios/rp-2017-08.pdf).

Many thanks.

Caio

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Multidimensional IRT models
parts:
Using a prior which restricts the range of the parameter space to be > 0 does not identify a model. You still need to impose the usual parameter constraints via the loading pattern. Think about a simple set of linear equations with 2 knowns and 3 unknowns. Knowing that the third unknown is positive still doesn't let you uniquely identify the system, it just tells you the infinite region it's associate with (not the exact point). The IRT model is the same here, so imposing lower/upper bounds or priors with bounded spaces is not sufficient for identification.

Phil

messages.author: de2c0368d9349f5a
messages.subject: Re: Multidimensional IRT models
parts:
Dear Phil,

I think that I understood your point but I see no relation with this issue of identifiability. I, kindly, disagree with you. In the paper that I have mentioned we have discussed some issues concerning the identification of mirt models (there are other details in another paper not finished yet and the Master's Thesis of my student, written in Portuguese). In all simulation studies that her performed,under these restrictions, the parameters were well recovered. When we fix the latent trait mean vector in zero and the covariance matrix as the identidity, only ortoghonal transformations are allowed in the linear latent predictor (a*theta). Therefore, due to the nature of the ortoghonal matrices (say T), any transformation as (a*T’*T*theta) will lead, always, to an a*=a*T’, with a different sign of “a” (provided that its components have the same sign), which is not allowed since we are restricting "a" to be positives. I am currently doing some other simulations and we can provide the related results.

Best,

Caio
